subject: Request: temporary adjustment to P2 response commitment during platform maintenance
messages:
From: Alan Chu <alan.chu@nimbushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health Ops <ops@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary adjustment to P2 response commitment during platform maintenance

Hi Mina,

We're planning a rolling database maintenance that will affect our production traffic during the nights of Apr 10-12 (UTC evenings). We're reducing our on-call capacity that week due to planned PTO across two engineers, and we expect an increase in noise (jobs restarting + cache warmups) that may produce multiple P2-level incidents.

Could Redwood provide a temporary variance to the P2 response SLA for our account (Nimbus Health) for the maintenance window? Specifically, we're proposing a change from your standard P2 8-hour response to a 12-hour window during Apr 10 20:00 UTC through Apr 13 06:00 UTC.

If a variance isn't possible, please let us know mitigation options you can put in place (additional routing, canary throttles, or a dedicated standby). Attached is our maintenance plan (high level) — happy to walk through it.

Thanks,
Alan
Alan Chu
Head of Platform Operations, Nimbus Health
alan.chu@nimbushealth.com

Attachments: nimbus-maintenance-plan-20270410-12.pdf (application/pdf, 220KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alan Chu <alan.chu@nimbushealth.com>, Nimbus Health Ops <ops@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary adjustment to P2 response commitment during platform maintenance

Thanks for the heads up, Alan — and for the extra detail in the attached plan. Internal: I need a quick sign-off on a short, time-boxed SLA variance and the operational conditions we require to accept it.

Summary of ask:
- Account: Nimbus Health
- Window: 2027-04-10 20:00 UTC through 2027-04-13 06:00 UTC
- Requested P2 response: increase from 8h -> 12h for that window only

Proposed Redwood mitigations (what I can commit to if we approve):
- Route Nimbus traffic to a warm standby pool for the maintenance window (reduces noise impact by ~60% in our tests).
- Enable automatic severity triage: only incidents with clear impact to payment or data loss escalate as P1. All other items treated as P2.
- Provide a documented escalation path: include APAC on-call fallback from 22:00 - 06:00 UTC to cover the overnight hours in the US.

Conditions for approval:
1) Nimbus opens a Jira ticket with the maintenance runbook (please link to RI-8421).
2) We receive a list of the two engineers (names) who will be on PTO so we can correlate alerts.
3) Update the Runbook with a pre-approved rollback plan (we've attached a delta doc).

If Ben/Marissa can sign off, I'll confirm with Alan and publish the temporary variance with an expiration timestamp.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Office: +1 (415) 555-0112

Mina — I reviewed the maintenance plan and the proposed mitigations. I'm willing to approve a provisional SLA variance under the following constraints:

- Variance: P2 response window extended to 12 hours only for 2027-04-10 20:00 UTC -> 2027-04-13 06:00 UTC.
- Expiration: variance automatically expires 2027-04-13 06:00 UTC unless a formal extension is approved.
- Runbook: Nimbus must add a clear rollback step and a named escalation (primary + secondary engineer) in RI-8421.
- Status page: Nimbus to publish a scheduled maintenance notice 48 hours prior.
- P1 unaffected: P1 response and on-call routing remain unchanged; P1 will still trigger immediate on-call paging.

Operational note: we'll enable the warm-standby routing and a short manual throttle (if necessary) during the first night to reduce noise. I'll also have one of our SREs on-call overlap for the first 6 hours of the window.

Approved by: Ben Carter, Senior Support Lead
